messages:
maria: Quick Q — running into issues with the Node/TS SDK in Next.js Edge functions and also in Vite dev builds. Edge logs show 'require is not defined' and Vite/ESBuild complains about node:buffer. Anyone seen this pattern?
jonathan: Yup, this is usually packaging/exports-related. Are we shipping a CJS bundle by default? Edge+Vite expect ESM and no node builtins.
maria: We currently build both CJS and ESM but package.json sets "type": "module" and main -> dist/index.cjs, module -> dist/index.mjs. Some bundlers pick the wrong field.
priya: Can you paste the package.json exports section? Conditional exports help a lot for edge/browser/require resolution.
maria: Here's simplified snippet from the current package.json: 
```json
{"main":"./dist/index.cjs","module":"./dist/index.mjs","type":"module"}
```
maria: No explicit exports field right now.
alex_g: That explains it. Without `exports` the bundlers/Node resolution can pick main even if they want ESM. Add an `exports` map with import/require/browser keys. Example: 
```json
"exports":{ ".":{"import":"./dist/index.mjs","require":"./dist/index.cjs","browser":"./dist/index.browser.mjs"} },"main":"./dist/index.cjs","module":"./dist/index.mjs","types":"./dist/index.d.ts"
```
priya: Also add a separate entrypoint for edge: "./edge": {"import":"./dist/edge.mjs","types":"./dist/edge.d.ts"} so you can `import { EdgeClient } from 'redwood-inference/edge'` and that bundle only uses fetch and no node builtins.
chris: For Vite specifically, if users bundle in dev it will try to bundle dependencies unless marked external. We should document how to configure `optimizeDeps.exclude` or `ssr.external` for Vite, but better: ship a tiny browser/edge ESM that is tree-shakable and avoids `crypto`/`buffer`.
jonathan: Streaming is another wrinkle. Edge runtimes expect ReadableStream/Response streaming via native fetch. In Node we sometimes rely on undici or `stream.Readable`. The SDK should expose two streaming surfaces: a web-compatible one (async iterator over chunks using web ReadableStream) and a Node one (with event emitter/stream).
maria: Example of the web-friendly pattern we'd like: 
```js
// user in Edge or browser
import Redwood from 'redwood-inference/edge';
const stream = await Redwood.chat.stream({ model: 'rwd-1' });
for await (const chunk of stream) { console.log(chunk.text); }
```
jonathan: Right. And implement internal runtime detection: if globalThis.fetch && typeof ReadableStream !== 'undefined' use the web path; otherwise import undici dynamically in Node: 
```js
async function ensureFetch() { if (!globalThis.fetch) { const { fetch } = await import('undici'); globalThis.fetch = fetch; } }
```
priya: Careful: dynamic import of undici in an ESM edge bundle would blow up if bundlers inline it. Make sure the edge entrypoint doesn't reference undici at top-level. Keep dynamic import behind a Node-only codepath.
alex_g: Also, add `exports` condition for `node` vs `default` so Node picks up a node-optimized variant that can include undici imports (or native fetch in newer Node), and `browser`/`edge` pick the lightweight ESM.
chris: For CJS consumers (older Node) keep dist/index.cjs with a small wrapper requiring the ESM via `createRequire` or build a proper CJS bundle. Some consumers still `require('redwood-inference')`.
maria: Good checklist: 1) add conditional exports with import/require/browser/node/edge 2) publish an `edge` ESM that avoids node builtins 3) expose web-first streaming API + Node-friendly fallback 4) update docs with Vite/Next config hints (optimizeDeps/ssr.external, aliasing to /edge entry) 5) add tests using Next Edge dev server and a Vite app.
jonathan: I'll open a draft PR that adds the exports map + edge entry and a small shim for fetch detection. Linking: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1234 (WIP). Ping @sdk-team for review.
sdk-bot: CI started for PR #1234 — build matrix: node14/node18/edge-bundling · status: running
priya: For docs, also include sample package.json for consumer apps that need to force ESM resolution: 
```json
// next.config.js (edge)
module.exports = { experimental: { runtime: 'edge' }, webpack: (cfg, { isServer }) => { if (!isServer) { cfg.resolve = cfg.resolve || {}; cfg.resolve.alias = { ...cfg.resolve.alias, 'redwood-inference': 'redwood-inference/edge' }; } return cfg; } }
```
alex_g: Small note: avoid `type: module` causing CJS breakage — keep it but ensure CJS main exists and exports map points require -> cjs. Or remove `type` and be explicit. Both approaches have tradeoffs.
chris: Should we provide a tiny `dist/edge.browser.mjs` that re-exports the core client but with no deps? That would be easiest for bundlers.
maria: Sounds like plan. Jonathan, assign me for docs and I'll add a Vite example repo.
jonathan: Assigned to @maria and @jonathan on the PR. I'll also add a smoke test using Next edge runtime in CI.
priya: Once merged, we should update the migration notes and call out that older CJS consumers should pin the CJS version or update to the latest Node.
maria: Thanks all — this helps. I'll follow up with the Vite example and a small section in QUICKSTART about edge vs node usage.
chris: :thumbsup:
jonathan: :rocket: will iterate on PR.
maria: closing loop — I'll post back here when drafts are ready.
